sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien language history. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: ANU (open, hdl:1885/146760).
sources.note: Comparative/historical, not a Bunu description. p.11: all Hmong-Mien languages tonal; W. Hmongic tone sandhi runs left-to-right. p.199 (sec. 4.2.1): Hmong-Mien nominal prefixes 'are unstressed, and in some languages they may harmonize with the nouns to which they are attached' (family-level remark; Meizhu Bunu prefixed nouns ku1-tau3 'tail', fa3-ɣe1 'stone', pi3-ntsau6 'nose' cited p.201). p.187: Bunu assigns its restricted sandhi tones to Chinese/Zhuang loans. No statement of where word stress falls in Bunu.

sources.citation: Strecker, David. 1987. Some comments on Benedict's 'Miao-Yao enigma: the Na-e language'. LTBA 10(2): 22-42.
sources.note: Saved (image-only, not scanned); comparative-lexical paper, not a Bunu description; not read for stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Bunu language' and 'Bu-Nao languages'; Wikipedia (zh) '布努语' (raw wikitext, 2026-09).
sources.note: English article summarises Meng 2001:32-37 (Qibainong Dongnu): consonant/vowel inventories, 8 tones plus 4 alternate (sandhi/loan) values 1'-4'; nothing on stress. Used for its bibliography (Meng 2001, Meng Youyi 2011, Meng 1996/2008 dictionaries).

sources.citation: Brunelle, Marc, James Kirby, Alexis Michaud & Justin Watkins. 2020. Prosodic systems: Mainland Southeast Asia. In Gussenhoven & Chen (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of Language Prosody. OUP (preprint halshs-01617182).
sources.note: Areal survey only: basic vocabulary monosyllabic 'in most Kra-Dai and Hmong-Mien languages'; no Bunu data, no Bunu stress statement.

sources.citation: Mortensen, David R. 2006. Logical and substantive scales in phonology. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley (already on file under hmon1264).
sources.note: Only Bunu content is verbal echo-reduplication data from Mao et al. 1982:94 (p.203); nothing on Bunu stress.

sources.citation: Strecker, David. 1987. The Hmong-Mien languages. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 10(2): 1-11.
sources.note: Classification overview (image PDF, scanned); lists Pu Nu (Tung Nu, Nu Nu, Pu No, Nao Klao, Nu Mhou); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Mao Tsung-wu & Chou Tsu-yao. 1962/1972. A brief description of the Yao language [Yaozu yuyan gaikuang, Zhongguo Yuwen 1962], translated in Purnell, Herbert C. (ed.) 1972, Miao and Yao linguistic studies, Cornell SEAP Data Paper 88, pp. 239ff. (section B 'Pu nu', pp. 243-244).
sources.note: Pu nu (Du'an) initials, finals, tones 1-8 plus 1'-3' (33 12 55 231 42 22 41 21 44 24 43); 'all tone sandhi values also occur only with these three tones'. The word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the volume; silent on word stress.
